results.evidence: _listed_files runs `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` and scan() reads those files and reports PATH:LINE. test_an_untracked_file_with_a_credential_is_reported builds a throwaway git repo, writes an untracked notes.txt with 'harmless' on line 1 and the SMTP_PASSWORD=hunter2 line (assembled from parts) on line 2, and asserts scan(repo) == ['notes.txt:2']. test_an_ignored_file_is_not_scanned shows .gitignore'd files are skipped. I ran `uv run --offline pytest -q -rs tests/test_no_send_credentials.py -v` and all 29 tests passed.

At HEAD the scan skipped its own file with `path.resolve() == this_file` (HEAD line 122), and the sample lines were literal. The working copy builds every sample line with `_sample(...)` from parts (lines 40-43, 60-69) and has no self-skip. `_scanned_files` (lines 137-146) only skips the `work/` planning records. `test_the_scan_reads_this_file` (line 165) asserts this file is among the scanned paths. I ran `find_credentials` over the file's own lines and it returned [], so no line matches. `uv run --offline pytest tests/test_no_send_credentials.py` passed 29 of 29.

With PATH=/nonexistent the scan test (-k listed) was SKIPPED, not errored: 'SKIPPED [1] tests/test_no_send_credentials.py:99: git is not on PATH; the R-27 credential scan lists files with git ls-files' (1 skipped, 28 deselected). The reason names git. The whole file passes normally with git present (29 passed), including test_the_scan_is_skipped_naming_git_when_git_is_not_on_path, which sets PATH to an empty directory and expects the skip. I ran the suite with the venv python directly because the `uv run` form was blocked by the read-only gate.
